name: 3D Spatializer
author: DSP Toolbox
description: Places up to 8 sources in 3D around the listener (binaural HRTF, for headphones). Uses Steam Audio (Apache-2.0).

paramHelp.output_gain_db: Overall level of the mix of all sources, after spatialization.
paramHelp.distance_atten: Sources get quieter with distance (inverse distance: 6 dB per doubling beyond the reference distance).
paramHelp.min_distance_m: Reference distance for attenuation: a source closer than this is not made louder, beyond it the level falls by 6 dB per doubling. Picking a range preset sets it (Near 0.1 m, Mid 1 m, Far 5 m). A small value makes close movement very audible.
paramHelp.air_absorption: Distant sources lose high frequencies, as in real air. Strength is set by 'Air absorption amount'.
paramHelp.air_amount: How strong the air absorption is, as a multiple of physical air (1x). Real air does almost nothing within a few metres, so the Near and Mid presets exaggerate it (20x and 5x) to make distance audible. Only the highest frequencies are affected, so try pink noise or hi-hats.
paramHelp.close_ild: Makes the difference between the ears bigger for a source close to your head (nearer than about 1 m) on the Steam Audio and Mid/Far sets: the far ear gets quieter and darker, the near ear a little louder. 0 = off, 1 = default, 2 = twice as strong. The Near range's own sets are measured up close and are not changed.
paramHelp.hrtf_interp:
How the head-related filter is chosen between the measured directions.
Nearest: uses the single closest measurement. Cheapest, but a moving source can step or flutter slightly as it crosses from one measurement to the next.
Bilinear: blends the four closest measurements, so movement is smoother (a little more CPU). For a source that stands still the two sound almost the same.
paramHelp.spatial_blend: 1 = fully spatialized (HRTF). Lower values mix in the plain, unprocessed signal; 0 = the original sound in both ears.
